claim_reviews.claim: Project epistemic architecture: append-only multi-model reviews, most-conservative-wins certification, hedged claims, disclosed AI collaboration, open code and data.
claim_reviews.evidence: The architecture works: earlier audits demonstrably forced real corrections (the v6 clipping demotion in CERTIFICATE.md, the Cohen-Lenstra h=1 correction, the inverse-square retraction, the Cayley/transitivity reframings), and the corrections are preserved rather than overwritten. Several pages (exception-hierarchy, A12-convergence, amplification, the three CFD pages) now meet a standard where every published number reproduces from a committed artifact.

sources.reference: docs/verifications/ ledger; paper/CERTIFICATE.md; per-finding correction notes

claim_reviews.claim: Data-preservation rule: every computation logs to a committed file (or HF dataset).
claim_reviews.evidence: Compliance is uneven and it is the single root cause behind most disputes in this audit: the transitivity sweep has no log; the Cayley BFS has no logs; the N=40 prime spectral CSV is cited but absent; the A123 10^10 headline log is a 225-byte partial; the class-number 27B '4.5 h' cluster run has no log while two slower committed runs contradict it; the 100k-point arb Dolgopyat dataset is absent while the committed 20k-point CSV contradicts the page citing it. Where the rule WAS followed (density logs, CFD CSVs, class-number histograms, kronecker analysis JSONs), my audit verified the pages essentially perfectly — the correlation between artifact discipline and claim accuracy across these 19 pages is near-total.

sources.reference: Per-finding reviews of this date, missing-artifact inventories

claim_reviews.concerns: Enforce the rule mechanically: no published number without a committed (or HF-hashed) artifact reference.

claim_reviews.claim: The published corpus is quantitatively accurate as it stands.
claim_reviews.evidence: This audit found, against the repository's own artifacts: (1) representation-growth — every sample value, the regression, and the hash contradict the cited CSV; (2) kronecker-s30 — the headline max g exceeds the exact S_30 dimension bound by ~28x and is mathematically impossible; (3) hausdorff — five of seven removal-cost rows wrong, one ordering physically impossible; (4) spectral-gaps — the 0.237 uniform floor is an N=15 Galerkin artifact that the repo's own N=40 logs move to 0.687; (5) framework page — the t>=2 Dolgopyat bound is violated 203 times by its committed profile, and the sieve inequality fails at its stated d=2 boundary; (6) cayley — three wrong group orders and a uint32 encoding that cannot address p > ~200; (7) phase-transition — 10^9 values under a 10^10 header and a wrong delta({1,3,5}). Most of these errors are in the pages' secondary or headline-summary layers while the underlying computations, where committed, are genuine — but in a computational-mathematics project the tables ARE the product.

sources.reference: Individual fable-5 reviews of this date (each dispute is artifact-cited there)

claim_reviews.claim: The strongest results survive independent adversarial recomputation.
claim_reviews.evidence: The results the project should be proudest of are real: the 27-exception set for {1,2,3} (replicated from scratch, witness-by-witness, exhaustively at the hard cases); the full digit-pair density hierarchy with its scale-dependence honestly disclosed; the A12 logarithmic fit reproducible to the second decimal of every residual; 30 billion class numbers whose every published percentage matches the logs and whose central conceptual correction is right; the S_40 restraint in refusing an int64-overflowing computation; and three CFD pages with complete artifact chains including a committed out-of-memory failure certificate.

overall_assessment: Audited as a whole, this is a serious computational-mathematics project with a working self-correction machine and a real, replicable core — and a persistent gap between its computations and its prose. Where artifacts were committed, my independent recomputation verified the pages at a level few preprints would survive (six regressions to the last printed decimal; discrete sets element-for-element under an independent algorithm). Where artifacts were missing or stale, the pages accumulated errors up to and including a headline value that violates an exact theorem-level bound (S_30 max g) and a headline floor refuted by the project's own committed refinement logs (spectral 0.237). The pattern is diagnostic, not moral: numbers copied into prose decay; numbers regenerated from artifacts don't. The fix is mechanical — publish no number a script can't recompute from a committed artifact — and the project already owns every tool needed to enforce it.
recommendations: Add a CI job that recomputes every quantitative table in bigcompute.science/src/content/findings from committed artifacts and fails on mismatch
Triage the two uncertified-recommendation pages first (representation-growth, kronecker-s30 max-g), then the spectral N>=40 re-sweep and the hausdorff table regeneration
Close the missing-artifact list: transitivity log, Cayley per-prime data, N=40 prime CSV, completed A123 10^10 log, class-number 27B cluster log, arb Dolgopyat dataset
Propagate the CERTIFICATE/CERTIFICATE_ERROR machine-readable exit-certificate pattern from the CFD kernels to all experiments
certification_justification: Project-level entries aggregate heterogeneous findings and should not carry a blanket certification; individual levels are recommended per finding. The project's process merits confidence; several of its published tables currently do not.
